# SEO-306: List only absolute HTTPS locations in llms.txt

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | `llms-txt` |
| Category | `EMERGING_GEO` |
| Minimum level | `RECOMMENDED` |
| Severity | `LOW` |
| Impact | `LOW` |
| Change safety | `SAFE_AUTOMATIC` |
| Evidence tier | `D` |
| Confidence | `MEDIUM` |

## Statement

Every location the file references is written as a complete address including the scheme and host, so a consumer that read the file without recording where it came from can still resolve each entry.

## Rationale

A relative path only resolves against a base the consumer may not have retained, and a plain-text file carries no element that establishes a base for it.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "has_llms_txt"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Expand each relative path against the production host at build time rather than by hand, so the file cannot drift from the host it is served on.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Parse the served file and report any referenced location that is not a complete address on the production host.
- Evidence: `FILE`, `HTTP_STATUS`, `BUILD_OUTPUT`
- Automated check: `llms-txt-absolute-https-links`

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `AI_ASSISTANT_RETRIEVAL`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: Expanding a path to an absolute address is mechanical and reversible, which is why it is permitted automatically. The convention it serves remains unrecognised by any documented consumer.
